items.prompt: YaB HIGH (bar-raise 2026-07-16): the Plaid sync insert at apps/api/src/plaid/sync.ts:95-103 uses `ON CONFLICT(plaid_transaction_id) DO NOTHING`, but db.ts:292-294 creates that index as PARTIAL (`... WHERE plaid_transaction_id IS NOT NULL`). Verified against the project's own better-sqlite3-multiple-ciphers build with the production schema: the bare conflict target fails at PREPARE time with SQLITE_ERROR 'ON CONFLICT clause does not match any PRIMARY KEY or UNIQUE constraint'. applyAdded therefore throws on the first page containing added rows; syncItem's catch (sync.ts:78-82) swallows it into status='error' and the cursor update at :72-74 is skipped, so the page replays and fails forever and Plaid rows never land. The plaid/ directory has no tests, which is why this shipped. Fix: add the index predicate to the conflict target (`ON CONFLICT(plaid_transaction_id) WHERE plaid_transaction_id IS NOT NULL DO NOTHING`) and add a behavioral test that prepares the real statement against a migrated in-memory DB. NOTE: fixing this alone exposes finance-product-dedupe-04 (pending-to-posted natural-key collision) - do both together. Ship via scripts/release.ps1.

items.evidence: apps/api/src/merchant.ts:14; apps/api/src/server.ts:487; apps/api/src/rules-engine.ts:74-75
items.prompt: YaB HIGH (bar-raise 2026-07-16, CHRONIC runsOpen 7): merchants whose descriptors carry a per-order token normalize to a unique string per transaction, so the categorization tail never shrinks for them. merchant.ts:14 strips `/\*+\d+/g`, which requires digits immediately after the asterisk. Executed against the shipped normalizer: 'AMZN Mktp US*2X4RT8901' -> 'AMZN MKTP US X4RT8901' and 'AMZN Mktp US*9K7QQ1122' -> 'AMZN MKTP US K7QQ1122' - it eats only the leading digit and leaves the order token attached. Every such transaction becomes its own Categorize row and, with the default-on save-as-rule, writes an exact-string rule (server.ts:487 stores body.merchant verbatim) that can never match another transaction, growing the rules table without shrinking the tail. Same class: 'SQ *', 'TST*', 'PAYPAL *'. Fix: strip the full alphanumeric token after an aggregator prefix (and any trailing alphanumeric order-id run) in normalizeMerchant so 'AMZN MKTP US' collapses to one merchant and one rule. Ship via scripts/release.ps1.
items.notes: 2026-07-17T02:36Z queue-drain-hourly: FIRST verification (never-attempted). CONFIRMED REAL - core claim and conclusion both hold, with two wording corrections worth carrying into the fix. (1) merchant.ts:14 does ship /\*+\d+/g. Executed the shipped normalizer verbatim: 'AMZN Mktp US*2X4RT8901' -> 'AMZN MKTP US X4RT8901' and 'AMZN Mktp US*9K7QQ1122' -> 'AMZN MKTP US K7QQ1122'. Both match the finding exactly - the pattern eats only the leading digit and leaves the order token attached, so every such transaction is its own merchant. (2) server.ts:483-487 does store body.merchant verbatim as the rule pattern (is_regex=0, match_field='normalizedMerchant'), and save-as-rule IS default-on (Categorize.tsx:27 useState(true)). So the unbounded rules-table growth is real. CORRECTION A: the finding calls the result an 'exact-string rule'; rules-engine.ts:73-76 actually matches by SUBSTRING (haystack.toUpperCase().includes(rule.upperPattern)), not exact equality. The conclusion is unchanged - a pattern carrying a per-order token can never be a substring of a different order's descriptor - but a fix that assumes exact-match semantics would be wrong. CORRECTION B: the 'same class: SQ *, TST*, PAYPAL *' claim does NOT reproduce as stated. Executed: 'SQ *COFFEE BAR SEATTLE WA' -> 'SQ COFFEE BAR', 'PAYPAL *STEAM GAMES' -> 'PAYPAL STEAM GAMES' - both collapse cleanly and are NOT affected. 'TST* PIZZA PLACE 4471' -> 'TST PIZZA PLACE 4471' retains a store number (the /\s+#\d+/ pattern only strips it when written '#4471'), which is stable per store and so does not grow the tail per-transaction. The bug is specific to descriptors carrying a PER-ORDER token, not to aggregator prefixes generally - scoping the fix to 'any aggregator prefix' would over-collapse distinct merchants (every SQ * merchant would fold into one). Repo state: HEAD a962350 (moved since the 2026-07-16 note's ba2ae66), working tree CLEAN. NOT APPLIED: auto_safe:false and the prompt says ship via scripts/release.ps1 = publishing, which is out of this task's no-publish scope. Kept PENDING for an attended YaB session. Fix is now de-risked: strip a trailing per-order alphanumeric run (require it to look like an order id - mixed letters+digits, length >= 6) rather than blanket-stripping the token after any '*', keep substring semantics in mind, and add a normalizer unit test covering both the AMZN collapse and the SQ */PAYPAL * non-regression before shipping.

items.title: Drive the Plaid takeover archive boundary from Plaid's real earliest_available_date so post-takeover history cannot double-count
items.prompt: YaB HIGH (bar-raise 2026-07-10): PlaidConnectFlow.tsx:92-94 hard-codes the takeover window to exactly 90 days back, with an in-code comment conceding "Phase 2 should ask Plaid for the real earliest_available_date". commitTakeover (plaid/takeover.ts:65-78) therefore archives CSV rows only WHERE posted_date >= that date, one-shot and never re-run, while Plaid backfills up to 24 months of the same history as source='plaid' (plaid/sync.ts:85-121 re-archives nothing). Neither unique index catches the overlap: CSV raw_description differs from the Plaid name, and CSV rows carry a NULL plaid_transaction_id. Every real transaction older than 90 days therefore appears twice in transactions_live and double-counts in all analytics. Fix: drive the archive boundary from Plaid's real earliest_available_date per item, or re-archive overlapping live CSV rows on each sync as older Plaid history backfills. Add a regression test covering a takeover with CSV rows predating the window. Live exposure is limited today because Plaid is Sandbox-only (D-012), but this bites the moment Production is approved. Ship via scripts/release.ps1.

items.title: photos storage bucket is enumerable by any client; exposes pending (unscreened) catteries' photos
items.detail: X:\YesAndCattery\supabase\migrations\0006_photos_storage_bucket.sql declares `create policy "photos public read" on storage.objects for select using (bucket_id = 'photos')`. A select policy on storage.objects governs LISTING, not just object fetches. The bucket is already public, so objects serve by URL without any policy - this policy buys nothing for display but lets any client call the storage list API and enumerate every object. Supabase security advisor flags it as public_bucket_allows_listing (WARN). Impact is project-specific: a cattery is deliberately not public until screened, yet photos are uploaded during the pending application, so enumeration exposes unscreened catteries' photos that RLS otherwise hides. items.evidence: Verified read-only at HEAD 1752caa on 2026-07-17. (1) auto_pause.gd:85 connect_wave_director and :95 connect_command_post have ZERO callers anywhere in source/ (auto_pause is referenced nowhere outside its own file). (3) The enemy_vision loop queries group 'enemies' via global.get_cached_nodes_in_group with NO add_to_group registrar anywhere in source/. (4) auto_pause.gd:114 types _command_post.global_position as Vector2 in a 3D world, so it will hard-error the day it is wired. (5) ROOT CAUSE: auto_pause._try_pause (auto_pause.gd:167-174) calls _game_clock.set_paused(true), but grep shows source/world3d/ never reads game_clock at all - world_3d.gd:906 _toggle_pause keeps its own local _paused bool. So even wiring the connects and the signal would leave auto-pause a no-op. Correcting the 2026-07-15 report: there is NO connect_economy function; the economy hooks DO wire in _ready via /root/economy and economy.gd emits building_destroyed (:762) and resource_shortfall (:319), so 2 of 4 toggles fire, not 0. The two dead ones are horde_day (defaults TRUE at options.gd:61) and enemy_vision. building_destroyed is connected but its emitter economy.record_building_destroyed (:748) has zero callers, so in practice only resource_shortfall ever fires.

items.title: Guard scrubDash against a blind em-dash strip in src/index.js (silent TICA parse break)
items.detail: MEDIUM/latent, canonical-audit 2026-07-17. src/index.js:1190 scrubDash reads: const v = decodeEnt(s).trim(); return !v || v === '-' || v === '—' ? null : v. decodeEnt turns TICA's — into a literal em-dash, so that branch is what nulls out dash-valued TICA fields (format, visitorNotes, comments at L1311-1315). public/app.js has already had its em-dashes stripped for the AI-tells voice rule; src/index.js has not. The obvious next move - 'finish the strip on index.js' - would rewrite that branch to v === '-', duplicating the condition and making every em-dash-valued TICA field return the literal string instead of null. Silent data corruption from a cosmetic edit. Fix: add a short comment at L1190 marking the em-dash as a required parsing literal (and/or a unit test asserting scrubDash('—') is null). Note the 2026-07-17 audit already applied the one genuine in-scope voice fix at L52, so no further strip of index.js is warranted; the remaining em-dashes there are comments, Discord separators, and placeholder glyphs. Solo-dev voice, no em dashes in prose. Ships with the pending Ring tree.

items.evidence: server.mjs:549, inside POST /script, builds the command "Remove-Item -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue '.git\index.lock'; & '<scriptPath>'" and runs it with cwd set to the TARGET repo. CLAUDE.md:30 forbids exactly this ("never blind-Remove-Item it") and mandates git-guard.ps1 Assert-GitSafe before any git write. Worse than a skipped guard: the delete runs immediately before invoking release.ps1 / push-to-github.ps1, which DO call Assert-GitSafe (push-to-github.ps1:7,40,45,70 + Confirm-GitIntact:74; write-dashboard-status.ps1:20,135,139,144,146). Their guard then finds no lock, concludes there is no race, and proceeds - so the preamble launders a live race into a clean-looking one and disables the abort path at git-guard.ps1:29-38. git-guard.ps1's own header records the damage this race has already caused: NUL-truncated .git\config and refs/heads/main knocked out of loose refs. Blast radius is cross-project: /script runs against any allowlisted repo (HBH, YaC, Gnosis, ...), and the portfolio runs concurrent unattended routines by design. UPDATE 2026-07-28 (canonical-audit-nightly): still present, unchanged, at server.mjs:548. NEW - this is now doc drift as well as a hard-rule violation: neither canonical doc discloses the Remove-Item preamble. DESIGN.md:70 (SS6) describes /script as running the two scripts 'locally (deterministic, no AI, no credit)' and ARCHITECTURE.md:56 says it runs them 'directly'. A destructive Remove-Item against another repo's git index is not 'directly', so a reader auditing the security posture from the docs alone would never find it. No separate doc item was filed: fixing the code removes the undisclosed behavior, and documenting it instead would be documenting a rule violation.
items.title: Agents /script blind-deletes .git\index.lock in the target repo, defeating the git-guard the handler mandates
items.prompt: Canonical audit 2026-07-24 (HIGH). X:\YesAndAgents server.mjs:549: the POST /script handler prefixes every run with "Remove-Item -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue '.git\index.lock'" in the target repo's cwd, then invokes that repo's release.ps1 or push-to-github.ps1. This violates CLAUDE.md:30 (never blind-Remove-Item the lock; use Assert-GitSafe from scripts/git-guard.ps1) and neutralises the guard inside the scripts it calls - they see a clean tree and skip the wait-then-abort logic that exists for exactly this race. DO: delete the Remove-Item preamble so the command is just "& '<scriptPath>'". The invoked scripts already clear genuinely-stale locks correctly via Assert-GitSafe, so the preamble is redundant with a safer implementation that already runs; removing it restores the abort. VERIFY: read scripts/git-guard.ps1 (Assert-GitSafe waits up to 20s for a live git process, then throws rather than writing into the race) and confirm push-to-github.ps1 still calls it on entry. DECISION for the implementer: whether /script should catch a guard abort and stream it to the phone as a distinct, readable error, or just let the script's throw stream through as ordinary stderr. auto_safe=false: it is a behaviour change on the remote-ship path plus a small UX call, so it wants an eyeball and a real /script run against a clean repo before shipping.

items.title: Section 6's globe locked decision omits the continent true-scale contract (ratio 1.00 of canonical E-W mileage, land held near 28 percent) that audit_globe.py checks every run
items.detail: The 2026-07-23 globe entry in section 6 records the shape-buffered cuts, tapered polar sizing, strict collision, no-orphaned-coastline, water-keying and label rules, and requires tools/globe/audit_globe.py to report zero hard-defect cells. It does not record the scale contract that v0.3.252-254 established and that the same script validates: every continent sits at ratio 1.00 of its canonical E-W mileage (Aldrgard 967 mi, Aestaria 1300, Titanoros 6667), holding land at about 28 percent against the 28.2 canon. That check is what caught the built sphere being wrong at 6.67 percent land when Titanoros had been capped at 77 degrees, so it belongs in the locked decision beside the defect-cell rule. Verified this run: audit_globe.py reports HARD DEFECT CELLS 0 and ratio 1.00 for every continent, with Titanoros i17 at 0.90 and i24 at 0.70 legitimately shrunk to fit. Note the authority for the canonical mileage, world/lore/world-scale.md, is itself a DM-gated page, so the spec should reference it as the gated source rather than restate the full sheet. ADDENDUM 2026-07-25: section 6 names only audit_globe.py as the pre-ship gate, but tools/globe/verify_coverage.py (added dd5355e) is now a second one: it walks every painted source land pixel and reports DROPPED (land no patch renders), DOUBLED (land two patches both draw) and HARD EDGE (a straight alpha wall cutting across land, the signature of a rectangular slice). Verified clean this run over 806,501 land pixels: 100 px dropped (0.012 percent, no blob above the noise floor), 117 px doubled (0.015 percent), no hard straight edges. Record it in the same section 6 edit as the true-scale contract. Note the i17 0.90 / i24 0.70 figures in the detail above are from 2026-07-24; as of 2026-07-25 the only island under design width is i13 at 0.80.

items.prompt: Agents MEDIUM (bar-raise 2026-07-24): the four hard rules that define this project's cost and security model - ANTHROPIC_API_KEY deleted at every spawn site (D-002), 127.0.0.1 bind default with a hard refusal otherwise (D-003), zero npm dependencies (D-004), prompts via stdin never argv (D-006) - have no automated verification. Every check is a human re-grep performed by the nightly canonical audit, which is why the audit report spends its first screen re-proving the same four facts. node:test is a Node builtin, so a test file breaches nothing in D-004. Fix: add a single test file (run with 'node --test') asserting that server.mjs deletes ANTHROPIC_API_KEY at all three spawn sites, that BIND_HOST defaults to 127.0.0.1 and the non-local-without-password path exits, that MODELS excludes fable and every spawn passes an explicit --model (D-008), that no package.json exists, and that no prompt string reaches argv. Then the nightly audit can cite a green run instead of re-deriving it, and a regression becomes impossible to ship silently.

items.title: Agents: the login rate-limit keys on caller-supplied X-Forwarded-For with no trusted-proxy check, so the lockout can be rotated away
items.evidence: server.mjs:296 - ip = String(req.headers['x-forwarded-for'] || req.socket.remoteAddress).split(',')[0].trim(), with no trusted-proxy check; loginFails is keyed on that value (server.mjs:220-228)
items.prompt: Agents MEDIUM (bar-raise 2026-07-24): the login rate-limit and five-failure lockout key on the first entry of a caller-supplied X-Forwarded-For header with no trusted-proxy check, so a caller who can reach the port can defeat the lockout entirely by rotating the header between attempts. Impact is bounded today because the server binds 127.0.0.1, the only ingress is the Cloudflare tunnel, and Cloudflare Access default-deny on a single email sits in front - an attacker has to get through Access before the password page exists at all. That is defense in depth working as designed, which is why this is MEDIUM and not HIGH, but the innermost layer currently contributes less than it appears to. Fix: trust the forwarded header only when the request carries a cf-ray (i.e. genuinely arrived through the tunnel) and prefer cf-connecting-ip when it does; otherwise key the limiter on req.socket.remoteAddress. Same pattern the /healthz caller check at server.mjs:282-290 already uses, so it is consistent with code that is already there.

items.title: Scheduler write-dashboard-status.ps1 blind-deletes the YaE git lock before Assert-GitSafe can see it
items.evidence:
CLAUDE.md forbids blind-rm of .git locks and names push-to-github.ps1 and write-dashboard-status.ps1 as already using the guarded path. They do not. Each clears the lock unconditionally BEFORE the guard: push-to-github.ps1:22-26 (first Assert-GitSafe at :80), write-dashboard-status.ps1:240-245 (Assert-GitSafe at :251), sync-audit-dashboard.ps1:104-107 (never dot-sources git-guard.ps1 at all). Assert-GitSafe (git-guard.ps1:16-42) implements the right logic - detect lock, check Get-Process git, wait 20s, throw rather than race - but by the time it runs index.lock and HEAD.lock are already deleted, so $present.Count is 0 and it returns immediately. The wait-and-abort path is unreachable for the only two locks that matter; config.lock is the sole lock it can still act on and nothing creates one. Two of the three scripts write to YesAndEverything, the repo every project's routines commit into concurrently. git-guard.ps1's own header records the consequence in past tense: that race has NUL-truncated .git/config and knocked refs/heads/main out of loose refs.

SCOPE NARROWED 2026-07-30 (audit-scheduler-nightly): commit 57f7bd2 fixed one of the three. sync-audit-dashboard.ps1:104-109 now dot-sources git-guard.ps1, carries a comment explaining why blind-deleting another repo's lock is wrong, calls Assert-GitSafe -RepoRoot $YaeRoot, and routes every git write through Invoke-Git; grep -l git-guard scripts/*.ps1 now returns four files, not three. TWO REMAIN, both re-verified unchanged at HEAD 57f7bd2: push-to-github.ps1:22-26 dot-sources the guard on line 20 then Remove-Items .git\index.lock on line 25, 55 lines before the first Assert-GitSafe at :80; write-dashboard-status.ps1:240-247 loops index.lock and HEAD.lock and Remove-Items both, four lines before its Assert-GitSafe at :251. Do not re-fix sync-audit-dashboard.ps1 -- use it as the pattern for the other two.
items.fix: Delete the pre-guard Remove-Item blocks at push-to-github.ps1:22-26 and write-dashboard-status.ps1:240-247, letting Assert-GitSafe adjudicate the lock instead. sync-audit-dashboard.ps1 already does this correctly as of 57f7bd2 -- copy its shape. Then reconcile CLAUDE.md: its blind-rm warning can keep naming push-to-github.ps1 and write-dashboard-status.ps1 as exemplars only once they actually are, and its three-step release.ps1 description is two steps short (write-dashboard-status and post-audit-digests are unlisted).
items.prompt: NARROWED 2026-08-02. Two of the original three files are already fixed: sync-audit-dashboard.ps1 in 57f7bd2 and push-to-github.ps1 in ffc1e45. Do NOT re-fix those. ONE file remains in this repo: X:\YesAndScheduler\scripts\write-dashboard-status.ps1 lines 240-246 loop over index.lock and HEAD.lock in the YaE tree and Remove-Item -Force each one, five lines before Assert-GitSafe runs at :251. The guard exists to decide whether a lock is stale or held by a live git process, and it can never see the lock because the script already deleted it. Deleting a lock under a live git process corrupts the index. Fix: delete the foreach block at :240-246 and let Assert-GitSafe adjudicate, matching the comment push-to-github.ps1 now carries at :22-24. SCOPE NOTE: the same pattern was found tonight in 18 other scripts across 9 repos, tracked separately as nightly-2026-08-02-portfolio-blind-git-lock-delete. Fix this one here; the sweep is that item.

items.title: Ring service worker precache and VERSION string both trail the app
items.detail: public/sw.js:3-7 SHELL installs ./data/seed.json but not ./data/scoring.json, which app.js:2467 fetches at boot alongside it - practical impact is near zero because the network-first .json branch at sw.js:41-51 caches it on the same first load, but the install manifest no longer matches the app's real boot set. Separately sw.js:2 reads VERSION = 'yar-v0.17.17' at app v0.17.19: nothing pins as a result (the shell went network-first in v0.17.16), but the string reads like a release-tracking cache-bust marker and is not one - scripts/release.ps1 bumps four places and never touches sw.js, while CLAUDE.md:90 tells a dev to bump it by hand. Fix both in one pass: add scoring.json to SHELL, and either have release.ps1 own the VERSION stamp or rename it to something that does not imply it tracks releases.

items.title: YaB CLAUDE.md still tells the reader to dismiss a release WARN that is now a real signal
items.detail: CLAUDE.md:87-89 documents 'release.ps1 "YaE ... failed" WARN is usually a false alarm' and instructs the reader not to go digging in YaE on the strength of it. That was true through v0.14.8: the spurious WARN came from PowerShell 5.1 wrapping a native git command's ordinary stderr into an ErrorRecord, flipping $? even on exit code 0. v0.14.9 and v0.14.10 added the shared Invoke-Git wrapper at scripts/git-guard.ps1:30-39, and write-dashboard-status.ps1 now routes its git calls through it and gates each WARN on $LASTEXITCODE (lines 265 and 273). A WARN today means the dashboard push actually failed. The handler now inverts the correct response. Rewrite the hazard section to say the artifact was fixed in v0.14.10 and a WARN should be investigated. Smaller companion: CLAUDE.md:80 credits the guarded lock path 'as of v0.14.4' without noting git-guard also supplies Invoke-Git as of v0.14.10. drift-auto-fix never edits CLAUDE.md, so this needs a hand pass.

items.title: Agents shipped v1.1.0 on 2026-07-16 but the last git tag is still v1.0.0 from 2026-06-23
items.prompt:
Version drift in Agents (working-tree-scan 2026-07-25). The version pill is internally consistent everywhere it is written by hand or by script - docs/DESIGN.md, README.md and status/data/Agents.json all say v1.1.0, and the 2026-07-25 canonical audit specifically notes the pill cannot drift by hand. The one source that disagrees is git: the newest tag is v1.0.0 on 0e5da81 (2026-06-23), so the v1.1.0 headless-auth-watch release from 2026-07-16 has no tag behind it.

This is the same shape as the Budget v0.10.0 case this routine used to carry, and it is worth resolving as a policy rather than a one-off, because Agents is the only repo in the portfolio with any tag at all - the other eleven ship purely on package.json plus CHANGELOG. Two coherent answers:

1. Tags are not part of the release contract. Then the stray v1.0.0 tag in Agents is the anomaly; either delete it or accept it as a one-time v1 marker and write that down in the Agents handler so the next audit stops reading it as drift.
2. Tags are part of the release contract. Then retroactively tag the v1.1.0 commit in Agents, and add the tag step to scripts/release.ps1 there and in the other repos' release scripts so this cannot re-open.

Pick one and make the repo match it. Do not leave the tag half-adopted - a single stale tag is worse than no tags, because it reads as a version claim that is fifteen versions of nothing behind the docs. Read-only note from the scanner: no code change is implied here, only the tag and whichever doc records the decision.

items.title: Cattery money-path comments claim destination charges; code does platform-hold + separate transfer
items.prompt:
Canonical audit 2026-07-25 (X:\YesAndCattery). Three places misdescribe how the escrow deposit is charged, and they contradict the code twelve lines below them.

What the code actually does (verified this run):
- src/index.js:220-228 builds the Checkout Session with mode 'payment', line_items, and payment_intent_data: { metadata }. There is NO transfer_data, NO destination, NO application_fee_amount. It is a plain platform charge.
- src/index.js:209-212 states the design and its reason: 'the charge goes to the PLATFORM - no destination, no application fee. Funds are held and later released to the breeder or refunded. The charge needs no Connect, so deposits work before a breeder has onboarded.'
- The breeder is paid at release by a separate POST /v1/transfers (src/index.js:299-302), amount = netTransferAmount(ctx.amount, ctx.application_fee).

What the stale text claims:
1. src/index.js:7-9 (file header): 'Buyers pay a reservation deposit via a Checkout Session with a DESTINATION charge: payment_intent_data.transfer_data.destination = breeder account, application_fee_amount = platform fee (0 for price-exempt breeders).'
2. src/index.js:199: '// POST /api/checkout  { kitten_id } -> { url } (Checkout Session, destination charge)'
3. CLAUDE.md:24-25: 'Stripe Connect escrow shipped (v0.25.1): destination charges, a $250 deposit, a 7% platform fee...'

PROJECT_SPEC.md:41-46 is already correct ('plain Checkout, no Connect needed'; admin releases via a Connect transfer). docs/STRIPE.md does not use the word 'destination'. So the canonical doc is right and the handler plus the money-path file's own header are the stale ones - the header almost certainly predates the switch to the hold model.

Why it matters: CLAUDE.md:26 tells every future session to 'reason carefully before touching src/index.js, the escrow RPCs, or the Stripe migrations', then hands that session a false model of the charge. Someone acting on 'it's a destination charge' could add an application_fee_amount and double-collect the platform fee - once at capture, once via netTransferAmount at release.

Fix: rewrite the src/index.js header bullet and the :199 docstring to describe the hold model (plain platform charge at Checkout, separate /v1/transfers at release, fee computed at order-create and stored on the order), and correct the CLAUDE.md bullet the same way. Comment-only in src/index.js - do not change executable code. Not auto-applied: src/index.js is the gated money-path file and CLAUDE.md is a handler file, which drift-auto-fix prohibits editing.

items.title: Section 4's 2026-07-10 locked map-pin decision is superseded by the v0.3.264 topographic pin scheme and was never updated
items.detail: Commit f11e5ef (v0.3.264) replaced the map's colour-coded pin model and touched PROJECT_SPEC.md only to bump the version pill. Section 4's locked decision still reads 'ONE shape for every kind, a small colored ring with a white halo, only the color changes by kind (city red, town orange, village gold, landmark violet, water blue, region teal)'. web/build.mjs now renders ten kind classes (city, town, village, mark, water, forest, relief, dry, ice, region) on a topographic palette, and settlement RANK is carried by symbol SIZE (--pd 17px city, 13px town, 10px village) rather than hue: all three settlement tiers are bone-white shades (#f6efe2, #e4d9c4, #c9bda6) and the code comment states outright 'that is why cities are not red here', since red means roads in USGS convention and hue is the wrong channel for an ordered variable. Also undocumented: per-kind legend filter toggles and an all-pins toggle (#pinlayer.hide-all). The shape half of the decision still holds (one ring, white halo, centered on the map art's own text, coordinate as ground truth). The rationale now living in the CSS comment is a better locked decision than the one in the spec; the question is only how Kane wants it framed and whether the 2026-07-10 quote is retired or amended.

items.title: The globe README's SE-volcanic-group section states a conclusion the newest commit overturned, and section 6 delegates its rationale to that README
items.detail: tools/globe/README.md ends on 'The SE volcanic group is NOT a defect (measured, 2026-07-24)', written by 11c475e, claiming the group correctly rides the mainland patch, the gap is 0.7 percent and invisible, cutting it out would move it for no visual gain, and only extremes past about 60 degrees still earn a patch. 39b5e6b, the newest commit, reverses all four and changed only CHANGELOG.md and the spec version pill. tools/globe/cut_titanoros.py now sets POLAR_LAT = 35 with Kane's own annotation: 'ASPECT, not size, is what breaks... 15% too narrow at 30, 31% at 40, 74% at 55... 35 deg is where the error passes ~20% and starts reading as visibly stretched. (An earlier note claiming a 0.7% difference compared two width multipliers and ignored this projection squeeze entirely.)' The earlier note being corrected is the README section still standing as current guidance. distortion_report.py, added by the same commit, opens with the same correction, and audit_globe.py now lists island patches at 38 to 42 degrees South, well inside the 'no patch before 60' rule the README still states. Fix: replace that section with the projection-squeeze rule (one equirectangular patch spans a fixed longitude range at every latitude it covers, so content riding the mainland is squeezed by cos(phi) against the patch centre; an island in its own patch is sized for its own parallel and escapes it), and note that POLAR_LAT is set from distortion_report.py's measurement.
items.impact: doc-accuracy
items.notes:
Not auto-applied: correcting it means authoring the replacement rationale, and section 6's globe locked decision points at this README as the rationale home. Related: memory gnosis-world-globe.

items.prompt: YaC HIGH (bar-raise 2026-07-25, reliability-04): A localStorage quota or private-mode rejection on the bag write is swallowed inside persist(), so the app confirms 'Saved.' / 'Photo saved' while the mutation silently evaporates on the next reload, and the one guard written to prevent that is dead code. src/main.ts:320-336 wraps localStorage.setItem(STORAGE_KEY, ...) in catch(e){console.error(e)} and never rethrows. Consequently src/bag-actions.ts:366-371 sets persisted=false in a catch that can never fire, making the 'Save failed - device storage error.' branch unreachable, and src/disc-photo.ts:75 toasts 'Photo saved' unconditionally after _persist() (src/disc-photo.ts:18-22, which also swallows). Photos are 512x512 JPEG data URLs (src/disc-photo.ts:15 TARGET_SIZE, :44 toDataURL) written into that same single STORAGE_KEY blob, so quota exhaustion is the realistic trigger. The only detector, src/mobile-hooks-6.ts:390-406, probes with a 1-byte write on a 30s interval and will succeed at the exact moment a multi-megabyte bag write fails. FIX: make persist() return a boolean (or rethrow) so callers can distinguish a failed write, and have the bag-actions and disc-photo toasts report the failure instead of confirming a save that did not land.

items.title: The Numbers tab documents a Sonic Pressure decay ledger the code does not implement, and the argument behind the locked per-shot values is false against the shipped build
items.evidence: The Numbers tab states passive decay four times: the thresholds preamble ("Decays at 0.5/sec passive, 1.0/sec with Watch Doctrine researched"), the reduction-sources table ("Passive decay -0.5/sec, Always on"), the steady-state ledger chart data array ({n:"Passive decay",v:-0.5} and {n:"Watch Doctrine (extra decay)",v:-0.5}), and the tuning-intent paragraph. economy.gd:381 sets SONIC_PRESSURE_PASSIVE_DECAY_PER_SEC = 0.0 with the comment "Base ships at 0 (SP is event-driven in v1)", and the applying branch is guarded if > 0.0. Watch Doctrine does not double decay: day_events.gd:184 subtracts SONIC_PRESSURE_CLIMB_BASELINE (0.5 per MINUTE) from the climb rate, cancelling the Existential dread baseline. lantern.gd carries no SONIC_PRESSURE reference at all, so the documented -1.0/sec hum suppression does not exist. The shipped model is a per-minute climb ledger (baseline +0.5, +2.0 no housing, +0.5 no walls, +1.0 under 50 Food, minus a 1/3/6 food-variety bonus). The tuning-intent paragraph reasons that a 10-Rifleman line at 0.375 SP/sec sits below the -0.5/sec decay so sustained fire is tax-neutral; with decay at 0 it accumulates without bound, so the justification for the locked per-shot values does not hold. The Progress tab already marks sp-decay todo, so the document contradicts itself.
items.action: Decide which side moves. Either tune a real passive-decay rate and make Watch Doctrine double it, or rewrite the Numbers tab around the shipped climb ledger. Either way the tuning intent behind the locked per-shot SP values has to be restated. Not auto-fixable: both directions are balance decisions.

items.title: The six Sonic Pressure movers that actually ship are absent from the canonical doc
items.evidence: sonic_pressure_events.gd implements the whole SP event layer and none of its values appear in GDD.html: per-casualty spike +2.0 (SPIKE_CASUALTY), building-destroyed spikes +5/+10/+15/+20 by max-HP tier (SPIKE_BLDG_*), the S-26 rapid-attrition burst (+15 base, +1.5 per extra death, cap +30, 5 deaths in a 30s window, 30s cooldown), and wave-repelled relief (-10 base, -2 per 10 enemies, cap -20). day_events.gd:18 adds -5 per day survived and enemy_base.gd:904 adds -1.0 per kill inside the hum. items.evidence: Three DESIGN sections commit to manager-set per-employee constraint overrides that do not exist. §3.2 (docs/DESIGN.md:80): 'Set per-employee max shifts per day and max shifts per week (default: 1 shift/day, hours-driven cap per week)'. §8.1 (:213) lists 'per-day max shifts (default 1)' among the auto-fill algorithm's INPUTS. §9 (:257) promises 'per-employee constraint overrides (max shifts/day, max hours/week)' in the manager side panel. Against the code: max_shifts_per_day is a hardcoded literal at apps/api/src/routes/schedule.ts:112 (`max_shifts_per_day: 1`), and the line directly above it reads `max_hours_per_day: settings.max_hours_per_day` - so it is the one value in that config block that ignores system_settings entirely. No max_shifts_per_day column exists on users, no system_settings key seeds it (migrations/0006_polish.sql:33-36 seeds only max_hours_per_day, ideal_hours_per_day, default_max_employees_per_shift), and no route accepts it. Separately, min_hours_per_week and max_hours_per_week are written exclusively by PATCH /api/me (apps/api/src/routes/me.ts:103-122) - self-service. The manager-facing PATCH /api/users/:id allowlist is display_name, email, is_admin and the two membership lists (users.ts:172-190), with no hours fields, so a manager cannot set an employee's hour cap at all. §3.2's 'hours-driven cap per week' phrasing is defensible; the per-day shift cap and the manager-override framing are not. The §8.1 instance is the costly one: it presents a hardcoded 1 as a configurable input, which sends a reader looking for a settings row that was never created.

items.evidence: PROJECT_SPEC.md:43 documents descFull as 'string <= 260 chars (back label, full poetic description)' and data/label-templates.js:70 sets descFullMaxChars: 260. data/herbs.json violates it on 43 of 199 records (21.6%), lengths 261-317. The cap is enforced in exactly one place and it is silent: src/ui/editor.js:693 autofills with (found.descFull ?? found.desc).slice(0, tmpl.descFullMaxChars), a hard character slice with no word-boundary handling and no ellipsis. The textarea maxlength at editor.js:145 only stops a user from typing past 260; the autofill path writes straight to state. 35 of the 43 truncations land mid-word, so the rendered back label ends in fragments: tarragon (267) renders '...Mexican varieties are mild subst' losing 'itutes.'; lemon peel (262) renders '...mulling spice. The bright pinc' losing 'h.'; long pepper (265) renders '...returning now via modern c' losing 'hefs.'. The other five capped fields (desc 120, historicUses 180, compounds 240, cautions 240, pairings 100) have zero violations. No test catches this: test-data-integrity.mjs runs 9 checks and none assert a character cap, so it sat undetected through four consecutive nightly audits.

items.title: YaB README layout block omits workers/, the project's only cloud component
items.detail: README.md's Layout block enumerates five directories (apps/web, apps/api, packages/shared, docs, data) and omits workers/, which holds the deployed Cloudflare Worker at webhooks.yesandeverything.com: four tracked files with their own package.json and wrangler.toml, and the only part of this project that runs anywhere other than the user's machine. Two sections earlier the README says the app is 'a small web app that runs on your own machine' and that 'bank data never leaves the box'. Both statements are individually true, since the relay is metadata-only under D-010 and never sees a transaction, but a layout block that enumerates the repo and silently drops its one cloud deployment leaves a reader with a materially wrong picture of the trust boundary. Fix is one line leaning on D-010's existing metadata-only framing, not a rewrite. Structural because it is a positioning call about how prominently the cloud piece appears in a local-first tool's front-door doc, and because root-README edits are on drift-auto-fix's never-auto-apply list.

items.title: Six uncommitted Budget edits strand a correction to the published security policy
items.detail:
X:\YesAndBudget has six files modified and uncommitted, none of them touched by a commit since 2026-07-16 and the oldest not since 2026-07-01: .github/workflows/security.yml, SECURITY.md, docs/DESIGN.md, docs/SECURITY_POLICY.md, scripts/README.md, scripts/release.ps1 (42 insertions, 15 deletions). No stash entries. The tree has been dirty across at least the last two nightly scans.

Why this is P1 rather than the usual P2 for a stale tree: docs/SECURITY_POLICY.md says of itself that it is mirrored at https://yesandeverything.com/projects/budget/security and that the mirror is canonical. The committed-and-published version of section 4 still reads 'Application-layer encryption is not implemented today; if added (see Wave 6 SQLCipher plan)...'. The uncommitted correction says the SQLCipher capability (Wave 6, D-008) is in fact implemented and tested but not engaged on this install, so nothing is encrypting the database file today and a migration command engages it. Both halves of that correction matter and neither is public: the published text understates what shipped and leaves a reader unable to tell that their own database is currently unencrypted. SECURITY.md and SECURITY_POLICY.md also drop the stale 'D-001 through D-011' decision range in favour of pointing at docs/DECISIONS.md as a whole, and security.yml's header comment is corrected from two jobs to three (audit, typecheck, tests) with an explicit note that the web package's tests do not run in CI.

Action: review the six diffs, commit them, and ship through scriptselease.ps1 so the yesandeverything.com security mirror picks up the corrected text. Per the BR/YaB release note, finish the commit through Bash if PowerShell-wrapped git stderr aborts release.ps1. If any edit is judged wrong, revert that file explicitly rather than leaving it sitting.

items.title: Enqueue writers keep emitting items with no `prompt`, which work-queue-runner cannot execute -- 62 items were stranded, rate is rising
items.detail:
work-queue-runner's SKILL.md documents `prompt` as the work spec ("Run the prompt. Treat the `prompt` field as the user request for this turn.") and its field table defines it as "Full prompt to run when the item is processed." There is no documented fallback to `title`/`detail`. But the audit-side writers (canonical-audit, bar-raise, handler-audit, drift-auto-fix) enqueue findings with title+detail and NO prompt, so those items are structurally undrainable and sit at attempts:0 indefinitely. The 2026-07-26T12:30Z hourly drain found 62 such pending items (59 never attempted) and backfilled a synthesized prompt into each (stamped promptBackfilledAt). That was a one-off repair, not a fix: the rate is ACCELERATING -- 13 promptless items added 2026-07-24, 16 on 07-25, 18 on 07-26 -- so the backlog regrows every audit cycle. The same defect stranded gnosis-release-62-proposed-dm-answers at attempts:0 for 9 days.

Recommended fix (cheapest, one place): give work-queue-runner an explicit documented fallback -- when `prompt` is blank, build the working prompt from title + detail + evidence + source rather than skipping the item. Optionally also require `prompt` on the enqueue side, but the runner-side fallback is the single change that makes every existing and future promptless item drainable. Kane's call on which side to fix; touching shared skill definitions is why this is not auto_safe.

items.title: Two live Locked Decisions at GDD.html:2909-2910 and 2913-2914 still instruct third-party asset-pack adoption from an _ARCHIVE tree deleted in v0.99.40
items.evidence: Both cards sit inside tab-decisions (opens 2559, closes 2962), so they are live Locked Decision cards, not changelog period record, and neither carries a supersession note. Card 2909-2910 'Isometric Realm Medieval = v0 placeholder pack' (2026-05-06) makes five wrong claims. (1) It names jpcu_Isometric_Realm_Medieval as the v0 placeholder source for buildings, walls, towers, farm tiles and trees; the pack was deleted from disk on 2026-07-10 in v0.99.40 and _ARCHIVE/ now contains only 'here-there-be-hordes' and 'starlightfurnace'. (2) It says the adoption pass S-33 brings them in via PowerShell manually; that is now forbidden, since docs/ASSET_PROVENANCE.md line 68 states 'Standing rule: no third-party asset packs in this project.' (3) It says real commissioned art replaces these in the M4/M5 polish window; all art is already own-team, Erik's 3D deliverables plus owner-made UI art. (4) It gives the pack location as X:\HereThereBeHordes\_ARCHIVE\..., which is wrong twice: the folder was renamed to X:\HereBeHordes at v0.72.0 and the directory was then deleted at v0.99.40. This line is the ONLY live-tab survivor of the rename sweep; the other four HereThereBeHordes hits in the GDD (4799, 4801, 4802, 4803) are all inside tab-changelog and are correct as period record. (5) It tells the reader to find tentative file picks by searching the Assets tab Notes column for 'Candidate:'; that string appears 0 times in the Assets tab. Card 2913-2914 'Asset dual-residence: every used asset lives in BOTH _ARCHIVE and assets/' (2026-05-07) is worse because it is an active instruction rather than a description: it tells the reader to copy assets from _ARCHIVE/ into assets/art/ and leave the original in place, with a worked example path inside the deleted Realm Medieval tree. CLAUDE.md line 56 already states the opposite in plain words, that the dual-residence rule is retired, so the handler and the canonical doc disagree and the canonical doc is the one a session is told to read first. Contrast establishing this is an oversight rather than deliberate period record: the five decision cards retired by the 2D-layer drop (2662 camera projection, 2706 AStarGrid2D pathfinding, 2799 the 60 px/s speed anchor, 2815 the SmallScale enemy sprite pack, 2840 the Node2D iso renderer) EACH carry an in-sentence supersession note pointing at v0.98.5 and the live 3D replacement, and Backlog row S-33 was closed 'done' with the note 'OBSOLETE: the sprite-pack adoption pipeline retired with the 2D layer'. So the same commit band that purged the assets updated ASSET_PROVENANCE.md, the README, the handler and the backlog, and missed only these two decision cards. The code side of the purge is clean: swept assets/ again on 2026-07-27 and found no surviving pack-derived file and no stranded asset path in any live tab. The defect is confined to policy prose.

Pattern worth keeping: the owner reliably annotates decisions when retiring a SYSTEM (all five 2D cards carry supersession notes) and reliably misses them when reversing a POLICY (both asset-pack cards, plus the publish card from a tooling change). items.title: The Numbers enemy Move column disagrees with the shipped speeds for seven of eight enemies and inverts the Leviathan
items.evidence: source/data/enemy_stats/*.tres is the authored source of truth (enemy_data.gd builds NUMBERS from it and apply_to_node writes it to both the Node and pooled paths). Shipped px/sec, as a ratio to the Shambler baseline, against the doc Move column: Shambler 18.0 = 1.0 vs 1.0 (agrees); Lunger 36.0 = 2.0 vs 3.5; Brinecaster 36.0 = 2.0 vs 1.6; Siren 43.2 = 2.4 vs 1.0; Wrecker 43.2 = 2.4 vs 1.4; Bilgemaw 50.4 = 2.8 vs 1.2; Shoaling 54.0 = 3.0 vs 4.0; Leviathan 64.8 = 3.6 vs 1.0. Only the Shambler agrees. The Leviathan is documented as tied-slowest, which reads as a lumbering boss and is how a counter would be designed, and ships as the fastest enemy in the game. Unlike the queued unit move-speed question this is not a uniform conversion factor: it changes relative ordering, so it is balance-facing.
items.action: Re-derive the Move column from the authored .tres values, or move the values. Decide alongside canonical-audit-2026-07-25-rising-move-speed-question-omits-halving so units and enemies land on one convention. items.title: The daily dashboard-sync task fails its own commit/push on every run: audit_dashboard.py exits 3 on the audit template's untagged 'Minor, grouped' heading
items.evidence: tools/audit_dashboard.py gained a _warn_unparsed guard in 0.58.1 that returns exit 3 when any drift item carries no readable severity. The project-canonical-audit report template emits exactly one such heading in every report by design: '### Minor, grouped'. Traced through scripts/sync-audit-to-dashboard.ps1:42-50, exit 3 is not the rc==2 'nothing to sync' case, so it falls to 'if ($rc -ne 0)', prints 'ERROR: audit_dashboard.py sync failed (exit 3)' and exits 1 BEFORE the commit-and-push block at :76-87. The Python rewrites the audit block on disk first, so the counts themselves are not wrong -- X:\YesAndEverything\status\data\Chains.json holds 2026-07-26's exact {critical:0,high:1,medium:4,low:4}. The failure is masked because a different task commits that file: git log on status/data/Chains.json shows the newest commit is 'f2dc3f8 status(Chains): bar-raise 2026-07-26', not an audit-sync commit. The audit counts have been reaching the live dashboard as a passenger on the bar-raise task's commit since 0.58.1 landed on 2026-07-24. Measured directly on the 2026-07-27 report before it was worked around: unparsed_items returned ['Minor, grouped'] and _warn_unparsed returned 3.
items.recommendation: Fix at the parser, not the report. Teach _HEAD_SEV_RX (or unparsed_items) to treat a heading that is explicitly a grouped/minor bucket as LOW rather than unparseable, or have the project-canonical-audit template stop emitting an untagged heading inside '## Drift found'. The per-report workaround applied on 2026-07-27 (retitling the heading to carry a '- LOW' suffix) clears exit 3 for that one file only; the next report from an unmodified template reintroduces it. Do not weaken the 0.58.1 guard itself -- it is correct and was written for the 2026-06-23 incident where a silent 0/0/0/0 masked a real CRITICAL. Note the risk being carried meanwhile: if bar-raise is paused, retimed, or removed, audit counts stop reaching the dashboard silently, which is the exact failure mode the guard exists to prevent.

items.title: DESIGN.md 5.2 documents open first-login auto-provision, but the Worker is invite-only and hard-refuses anyone without a pre-seeded row
items.evidence: DESIGN 5.2 (docs/DESIGN.md:136-146) says 'There is no admin create account button' and 'if absent inserts a new row', closing with 'Anyone with an email can land in users'. loadOrCreateUser (apps/api/src/middleware/auth.ts:115-212) has four branches and only one inserts: (1) returning user by supabase_user_id :120-133; (2) invited user matched on email_lower where supabase_user_id LIKE 'pending:%', claimed via UPDATE :138-160; (3) INSERT only when the email is in INITIAL_SUPER_ADMIN_EMAIL / INITIAL_ADMIN_EMAIL :166-193; (4) everyone else hits console.warn('no invite slot') and returns null :170-174. Because authMiddleware treats null the same as no token (:32-33), a genuinely Supabase-authenticated stranger gets 401 unauthenticated on every route. The row 5.2 says the Worker creates is actually created in advance by an admin via POST /api/users/invite (routes/users.ts:278, seeding pending:<email> at :364), surfaced in the SPA as components/InviteUserPanel.tsx -- the exact button 5.2's first sentence denies exists. DESIGN 16 (:402) already documents that endpoint and its first-sign-in claim mechanic correctly, so 5.2 contradicts 16 and 3.3. Steps 4-5 of 5.2 (pending gate page, admin assigns sub-departments, gate clears) are still accurate for invited employees; the 'pending' flag is computed as described at auth.ts:36-42.
items.recommendation: Rewrite 5.2 against the invite-first model: an admin invites via POST /api/users/invite, which seeds a users row with supabase_user_id = 'pending:<email>'; the first magic-link sign-in claims that row by email_lower and attaches the real Supabase UUID; no invite slot means a hard 401, indistinguishable from unauthenticated. Strike 'There is no admin create account button' and 'Anyone with an email can land in users'. Keep steps 4-5 (pending gate, admin assigns sub-departments) as-is and cross-reference 16's invite endpoint. Env-seeded super-admin bootstrap stays the one auto-insert path (see 5.3). Structural because it needs the sequence authored, not a phrase swapped.

Keep steps 4-5 (pending gate page, admin assigns sub-departments from /admin/users, gate clears) -- those are still accurate, and the 'pending' flag is computed as described at auth.ts:36-42. items.prompt:
Yes& Apothecary [MODERATE]: the v0.8.0 cache-bust contract has three holes. Three modules are served at bare, un-versioned URLs on every page load and are never cache-busted, and three more are downloaded and instantiated twice per load. Proven by a live network capture, not inference.

index.html says the contract covers the whole graph: "Both the entry script and all its dynamic imports carry the build as a ?v= query, so Cloudflare's edge cache can't ever serve a stale module graph after a deploy". The stamping half genuinely works (scripts/release.ps1:250-260 rewrites window.__APOTHECARY_BUILD every release; the value tracks correctly across the last three releases), and src/main.js:8 appends V to all thirteen of its dynamic imports. But the graph does not end there: six modules are pulled in with plain static import statements, which resolve to bare URLs the stamp never touches.

Captured off the wire serving the repo over HTTP:
  NOT cache-busted at all (bare URL only):
    src/util/autofit.js        <- src/render.js:17
    src/util/print.js          <- src/ui/editor.js:10
    src/util/saved-labels.js   <- src/ui/saved-labels-ui.js:6
  Fetched twice, once with ?v= and once bare (two module instances):
    src/state.js               <- src/util/migrate.js:12
    src/util/persist.js        <- src/util/saved-labels.js:3
    data/label-templates.js    <- src/render.js:18 and src/state.js:18

Why the first three matter: a release that changes saved-labels.js ships a fresh saved-labels-ui.js?v=<new> against whatever copy of saved-labels.js the edge or browser already holds, because that URL did not change. The two are tightly coupled - the UI calls listSaved, saveLabel, loadLabel, deleteLabel, duplicateLabel, renameLabel straight across the boundary. Version skew there is a broken saved-labels panel, which is exactly the failure the contract was written to prevent. autofit.js (text fitting for both preview and print stage) and print.js have the same exposure with a smaller blast radius. This is a hazard on the NEXT release touching those three files, not a live defect today: the currently deployed graph is self-consistent.

Why the double-loads are lower severity: distinct URLs are distinct module records per the ES module spec, so each is evaluated twice. Two carry module-level mutable state - state.js:63 'let zoneIdCounter = 0' and persist.js:33 'let autosaveWarned = false'. Neither diverges visibly today, because defaultLayout() passes an explicit id: for every seeded zone (state.js:86-88) so the counter is never incremented on the bare instance, and a duplicated autosaveWarned at worst repeats one storage warning. Today's cost is three redundant fetches plus two latent split counters. It becomes a real bug the first time either counter is relied on for uniqueness across both instances.

Pick one direction:
1. Route the three un-versioned modules through ?v= by dynamic-importing them from main.js and passing them via ctx. This matches the pattern src/ui/editor.js:11 already describes ("cross-module references for cache-bust safety travel through ctx") - note editor.js:10 then violates its own line 11 with a static import of util/print.js. Consistent with existing architecture; more call-site churn.
2. Keep the static imports and have release.ps1 stamp the build query into the static specifiers too. Fewer moving parts at the source level, but it puts a source rewrite in the release path, which is a heavier thing to own.
Either way the three double-loads resolve as a side effect, since the duplication exists only because the same module is reachable by two spellings.

After the change, re-verify by serving the repo over HTTP and re-reading the network log: every src/ and data/ .js request should carry ?v=<build>, and no module should appear twice. Do not declare it fixed off a code read - the whole reason this sat undetected is that it is only visible in the request list.

Related and worth doing in the same pass if cheap: PROJECT_SPEC.md documents the cache-bust contract nowhere - not §3 Architecture, not §6 Renderer contract, not §8 Locked decisions - while four source files defer to it in comments (main.js:3, main.js:101, editor.js:11, migrate.js:10). Add it to the canonical doc so the invariant is recorded somewhere a future session will look. index.html's comment was corrected on 2026-07-27 to describe the partial coverage honestly; update it again once coverage is actually complete.

items.title: Ring status writer publishes .project-context.json remaining[] verbatim to a public dashboard card
items.detail: scripts/write-dashboard-status.ps1 lines 72-73 copy .project-context.json completion.remaining[] straight into itemsLeft.items in X:\YesAndEverything\status\data\Ring.json, which is committed to a public GitHub repo and served from the site (/status/ is only Disallow'd in robots.txt, which is not access control). The fifth entry is 1,383 characters of internal security narrative and currently publishes: (a) "OPEN: ... move view-as/sharing reads to DEFINER RPCs", an open hardening gap in a live app, also queued as bar-raise-2026-07-24-ring-viewas-sharing-definer-rpcs; (b) "leaked webhook revoked, rotation runbook"; (c) "KANE ACTION: recreate Ring Resources Bot webhook (release digests currently fail with 'Invalid URI' from the placeholder file)". No credential is exposed and nothing is exploitable on its own, but this is the same class of leak the portfolio already guarded on the barRaise field, reaching the same file through a field that was never guarded. Fix belongs in the writer (a leak guard, or publish a public-safe summary line instead of the raw note), not only in the note text, or the next context edit re-publishes it. Structural: it changes what a public surface publishes and needs a call on guard-versus-summarize. Likely affects the sibling projects' writers too, but this item is Ring-scoped.
items.notes: Auto-enqueued by canonical-audit-ring 2026-07-27, finding 1. Related: status-json-is-public-surface guidance, and the already-queued bar-raise item naming the same DEFINER-RPC gap.

items.title: PROJECT_SPEC domain section never states the best-50/30 ring cap that drives the headline number
items.detail: PROJECT_SPEC.md lines 36-55 cover ring types, the two point tables, the May 1 - April 30 season boundary, per-judge average score, and moving targets, but never state that only a cat's best 50 rings (30 for kittens) count toward its annual score. The rule is real and load-bearing in code: public/app.js:150 bestN() drives the Regional-points tile (app.js:472), a "Top-50 cutoff" stat tile (app.js:474), the cat page (app.js:1297), and the user-facing guide paragraph (app.js:1340). .project-context.json names it ("best-50/30 cap") and data/ANSWERS.md does not mention it either. A rule that changes the headline number a user reads belongs in the domain spec that claims to be the source of truth for scoring. Structural: it extends the canonical domain section and the wording should be Nick's, not auto-generated. Worth adding to data/ANSWERS.md as well if Pam confirmed the 30-for-kittens split.
items.notes: Auto-enqueued by canonical-audit-ring 2026-07-27, finding 3. items.impact: Two code paths disagree about the backups directory, one honoring configuration the other ignores. Not live on the current install; bites when the in-repo DB is absent or YAB_BACKUP_DIR is set, at which point a factory reset can leave complete database copies on disk.
items.title: YaB factory reset deletes the wrong backups directory; SECURITY_POLICY promises no copy survives
items.detail:
Two code paths resolve the backup directory and they disagree. apps/api/src/backup.ts:14 sets BACKUP_DIR = process.env.YAB_BACKUP_DIR ?? resolve(dirname(DB_PATH), 'backups'), so it follows the live DB and honors an env override. The factory-reset handler at apps/api/src/server.ts:1491 instead hardcodes resolve(dataDir, 'backups').

REVISED BY THE 2026-07-28 AUDIT. Three corrections to the original write-up, which together lower both the severity and the effort:

1. The stated blocker was wrong. backup.ts:167 DOES export an accessor: export function backupDir(): string { return BACKUP_DIR; }. server.ts already imports it at :60 and already calls it at :1142 for the backups-list endpoint. The fix is one line in the same file: const backupsDir = backupDir();. No new export, no API change, no fork in approach.

2. The divergence is not live on this install. db.ts:20-42 gives the in-repo database precedence: YAB_DB_PATH takes effect only when data/yesandbudget.db is absent, and db.ts:30 logs a warning when it ignores a set-but-overridden env var. The in-repo DB exists and is current (548 KB, written 2026-07-25), so DB_PATH resolves in-repo and both code paths land on the same directory. YAB_BACKUP_DIR is set nowhere outside backup.test.ts:19.

3. X:\.budget\ is not the counterexample originally cited. It exists, but under repo-precedence it is not the live install: its database is from 2026-05-21 and its WAL from 2026-05-23, both stale by two months. Its backups/ directory is empty, as is data/backups/. There were no snapshots anywhere on the machine at audit time, so there is currently no data for a reset to leave behind by this path.

What remains is a real defect: two paths disagreeing about one directory, one of which ignores configuration the other honors. It bites when the in-repo DB is absent (so YAB_DB_PATH engages) or YAB_BACKUP_DIR is set. Once server.ts uses backupDir(), the docs/SECURITY_POLICY.md:62 guarantee is true as written and needs no edit.
items.prompt:
In X:\YesAndBudget, make the factory-reset handler use the backups directory the rest of the api already uses.

One-line fix: at apps/api/src/server.ts:1491 the handler computes const backupsDir = resolve(dataDir, "backups"), which ignores both YAB_BACKUP_DIR and the resolved DB location. apps/api/src/backup.ts:167 already exports backupDir(), and server.ts already imports it at :60 and calls it at :1142. Replace the hardcoded derivation with const backupsDir = backupDir();.

Then add a test pinning that factory reset targets the same directory backup.ts writes to, including when YAB_BACKUP_DIR is set. Existing tests live alongside the api source; follow the surrounding vitest conventions (backup.test.ts:19 shows the env-override pattern).

docs/SECURITY_POLICY.md:62 needs no edit once this lands: the guarantee becomes true as written. Do not narrow the sentence instead of fixing the code, and do not do both.

Do not delete X:\.budget\ or anything inside it at any point. Do not run scripts/release.ps1 or bump versions. Solo-dev voice on any doc text: no first-person collective, no AI vocabulary, no em dashes.
items.notes: Re-rated high -> medium and re-scoped structural -> one-line by the 2026-07-28 audit. The original HIGH rested on a live divergent configuration that does not hold under db.ts repo-precedence, and on a missing export that in fact exists. Still worth fixing: the two paths genuinely disagree.

items.impact: Every front-door document for a local-first tool omits its one operator-controlled cloud component, so an external reviewer scopes the attack surface wrong.
items.title: YaB front-door docs erase workers/plaid-webhook-relay; decide once and apply to README + SECURITY.md
items.detail:
Three documents independently drop workers/plaid-webhook-relay/, the deployed Cloudflare Worker at webhooks.yesandeverything.com and the only part of this project that runs off the user machine.

1. README.md Layout enumerates five directories and omits workers/. Already queued separately as canonical-audit-2026-07-26-yab-readme-omits-workers (P3); fold that item into this one.
2. SECURITY.md:30, under 'What we do not provide': 'We do not maintain a hosted service. There is no operator-controlled production system to scan or harden.' The relay is exactly that, with its own package.json and wrangler.toml. This sits in the section a security reviewer reads to scope their review.
3. docs/SECURITY_POLICY.md:31 claimed a single outbound host. FIXED 2026-07-27 by the drift-auto-fix pass, which now names both the Plaid API and the relay. Listed here only so the set is complete.

Each omission is individually defensible as brevity. Together they mean every document an outsider reads describes a local-first tool with no cloud footprint at all. The adjacent promise at SECURITY.md:23 (no consumer financial data to any operator-controlled server) is carefully worded and true; the D-010 metadata-only framing is the thing to lean on.
items.prompt:
In X:\YesAndBudget, decide how prominently the webhook relay appears in the front-door docs, then apply that decision consistently.

Context: workers/plaid-webhook-relay/ is a deployed Cloudflare Worker at webhooks.yesandeverything.com. It is the only part of this project that runs anywhere other than the user machine. Under D-010 it is metadata-only: KV holds (item_id -> relay_key) maps and short-lived event queues, never tokens or transactions. apps/api/src/plaid/relay.ts calls it at :33 (register), :47 (deregister) and :60 (poll events).

Two places still omit it:
  - README.md 'Layout' block: five directories listed, workers/ absent, two sections after the line 'Bank data never leaves the box.'
  - SECURITY.md:30: 'We do not maintain a hosted service. There is no operator-controlled production system to scan or harden.' This is false as written.

This is a positioning call for Nick, not a mechanical edit: how visible should the one cloud component be in a tool sold as local-first? Ask him if it is not obvious. Whatever he picks, apply it to both files in one pass so they agree. Note that docs/SECURITY_POLICY.md:31 was already corrected on 2026-07-27 and now names both outbound destinations; match its framing.

Do not weaken the true claim at SECURITY.md:23 (no consumer financial data reaches any operator-controlled server) while fixing the false one at :30. Supersedes canonical-audit-2026-07-26-yab-readme-omits-workers; mark that item done when this lands. Do not run scripts/release.ps1 or bump versions. Solo-dev voice: no first-person collective, no AI vocabulary, no em dashes.
items.notes: Supersedes canonical-audit-2026-07-26-yab-readme-omits-workers (P3). Third sighting of the same pattern.

items.detail: .github/workflows/security.yml:51 runs `pnpm audit --audit-level=high --prod`. That command exits 1 today on GHSA-gcfj-64vw-6mp9 (axios >=1.15.2 <1.18.0, patched >=1.18.0), reached via apps/api > plaid@42.2.0 > axios@1.17.0. `gh run list --workflow=security.yml` shows failure on every run from 2026-07-25T03:34:10Z through 2026-07-27T11:18:09Z (9 runs, main and dependabot branches); the last success was 2026-07-20T11:13:51Z. A second HIGH, GHSA-r28c-9q8g-f849 (postcss <=8.5.17, patched >=8.5.18), shows in the dev-inclusive audit via vite/vitest; it does not fail the --prod gate but is the same one-line remedy.

items.title: Harden every push-to-github.ps1 against the PS5.1 git stderr-wrap (Invoke-Git guard)
items.prompt: Harden every project's scripts/push-to-github.ps1 (and any release.ps1 that calls git directly) against the PowerShell 5.1 stderr-wrap: git writes benign 'LF will be replaced by CRLF' and 'To https://...' lines to stderr, which PS 5.1 under $ErrorActionPreference='Stop' promotes to a terminating NativeCommandError, aborting the release AFTER committing but BEFORE the push completes and stranding completed work in the working tree. Apply the git-guard.ps1 Invoke-Git wrapper already used by YesAndBudget (relax EAP to Continue around each git call, check $LASTEXITCODE instead of trapping stderr; see memory yab-dashboard-push-warn-false-alarm). Repos to verify/fix: YesAndEverything, YesAndChains, HereBeHordes, BrackishRising, YesAndRing, YesAndCattery, YesAndGnosis, YesAndScheduler, YesAndAgents, YesAndApothecary (Budget already has it). For each: adapt git-guard.ps1, route git add/commit/push through Invoke-Git, then TEST with a trivial doc change through release.ps1 end-to-end and confirm the push lands (git log --oneline @{u}..HEAD empty) with NO Bash fallback. Removes the need for the ship-and-verify Bash workaround now baked into the burndown/drain routines.

items.title: Skylight can create a mis-owned event but has no way to correct one
items.detail: X:\YesAndSkylight has no way to correct an event filed to the wrong person, and mis-filings are designed in rather than accidental. src/owners.ts:59-65 inferOwner() deliberately falls back to owner=family when it cannot infer one from an inbound email subject/body, and DESIGN.md D14 accepts that trade-off explicitly (a shared event shown to everyone beats one silently filed to a person). So the email front door will keep producing events on the family calendar that belong to Nick or Lexi. Nothing in the project can move them: src/google.ts exports only createEvent() and probe() -- no move, update or delete; DESIGN.md section 6 has no corrective route (POST /api/quick-add only creates); src/ui.ts is a create-only form. Evidence that this bites in practice: commit c2fc67d records that 'Project ChainGrip Pure' (13 Aug) was sitting on the family calendar, is Nick's, and had to be moved to the Nick calendar on 2026-07-25 by hand via Google's events.move API, run outside this Worker. The limitation is now documented in DESIGN.md section 8 (applied by the 2026-07-28 drift-fix pass); this item is the capability itself. Deciding WHICH surface gets it is the structural part: (a) a POST /api/reassign route taking an event id + new owner and calling events.move, (b) a control in the PWA, or (c) no code at all -- just a documented events.move curl recipe in README.md. Option (c) is the cheapest and may be sufficient for a family tool. Whichever is chosen, note the wall's badge letter follows the Skylight profile the destination calendar maps to, so a move fixes the badge too.

items.impact: Every mis-filed event needs a manual trip to Google Calendar or a hand-rolled API call. The email front door guarantees these recur, so the manual work is ongoing rather than one-off.
items.drainNote: Needs an attended pass: choosing between an API route, a UI control, or a documented events.move recipe is a design call on a repo a parallel session owns. Do not add a write path unattended.

items.title: 236 questions marked (secret) render in full, marker and all, on 121 public entity pages
items.detail:
PROJECT_SPEC.md section 6 routeQuestion rule 3 sends a question the DM marked (secret) to /questions-dm, and the same section's stated reason for that page is that players never see it. The routing works: 0 of the 357 public questions.json records carry the marker. But the question TEXT is not routed anywhere. It renders inline on its own entity page, and those pages are public.

Measured 2026-07-28 against a fresh build: 236 (secret)-marked question lines sit on non-secret vault entities, and web/dist renders the literal string '(secret)' 274 times across 121 public pages. Worst offenders: /lore/the-coiled-guardian 14, /locations/mithralholm 12, /locations/cinderfall 8, /locations/ovicor 8, /locations/brasshollow 7, /locations/the-coldwood-march 7, /lore/the-aestral-reckoning 7.

Concrete example, fully readable on /locations/mithralholm without the DM cookie: 'Are the eggs chromatic (evil-blooded) hatching among metallic dragons, and what does the Hoard do about them? (secret)'

Two problems that want different answers.

ONE, the routing is defeated. Marking a question (secret) moves it off the player board but not off the player-visible web. Either the marker should also suppress the question from the public entity render, or section 6 should stop describing the DM queue as content players never see and say plainly that the marker is a board-sorting device only.

TWO, the authoring marker leaks into rendered prose. Even if the question stays public, (secret) is build-time routing syntax, not world prose. The sibling markers do not leak: (dm) and (player) appear 0 times in the built site. This half is a rendering defect on its own terms and is cheap to fix in the question harvester in web/build.mjs.

Severity medium, not high: the affected questions live on entities Kane deliberately left public and no secret: true entity content is exposed, so this is an intent-versus-implementation gap in the spec rather than a live spoiler leak.
items.impact: correctness
items.notes: Intent-versus-implementation gap, not a live leak of secret: true content. Part two (strip the raw marker from rendered prose) is mechanical; part one needs Kane.

items.title: 689 public-page question chips link to /questions-dm, which is a 401 dead end for players
items.detail:
Every answered-question chip on a public entity page links to /questions-dm#q-<qid> with the title 'See this on the questions page'. That path is in web/dm-paths.mjs, so the worker 401s it for anyone without the DM cookie.

Measured 2026-07-28: 689 such links across 215 public built pages. That is 97 percent of all public-to-gated links on the site (712 total); the other 23 are the DM-badged type-index rows and the blessed Maevyn transcript exemption, both sanctioned by the section 6 locked decision.

No content leaks. The target 401s and the chip label is just the word 'answered', so this is a UX defect rather than a security one. It is filed separately from the (secret)-marked-questions item because this half is mechanical where that one is a design call.

The fix is to route the chip to /questions when the question landed on the player board and to render the chip unlinked when routeQuestion sent it to the DM queue, so a player never clicks through to a 401.
items.impact: usability
items.notes: Pure UX. Target 401s so nothing leaks. Mechanical fix, no Kane decision needed.

items.title: The globe cutter leaves orphaned island textures on disk when the island set is re-cut
items.detail:
web/assets/globe/titanoros-i24.webp and titanoros-i24-labels.webp sit on disk unreferenced. web/build.mjs and tools/globe/audit_globe.py both run i1 through i23; disk carries i1 through i24.

This pair has now been in three states across three days: orphaned on 2026-07-26, live again on 2026-07-27 (which is why the queued deletion filed on the 26th was correctly killed as destructive before it could run), and orphaned again on 2026-07-28 after the island set was re-cut.

The two files are about 99 KB together, so the disk cost is nothing. The real finding is the pattern: while the cutter is under active iteration, any queue item naming specific generated assets rots into a destructive instruction within a day. THIS ITEM IS NOT A REQUEST TO DELETE THOSE TWO FILES. Deleting a texture that the next re-cut promotes back into use breaks the globe, which is exactly the trap the 2026-07-26 item set.

The durable fix belongs in the cutter itself: after it writes its patch set, it should reconcile web/assets/globe/ against the indices it just emitted and clean up or report what is left over, so the orphan can never outlive the run that created it.
items.impact: maintainability

bar-raise-agents and bar-raise-everything sharing a stamp to 4ms (.154Z / .158Z) as proof of a
"marked fired, never spawned" bulk write. That PAIR HAS NOW SPLIT: agents ran on 07-30, everything did
not. A shared millisecond stamp therefore does not mark a task as permanently phantom, and whatever is
holding apothecary and everything back is specific to those two rather than a property of the 07-29 bulk
write. Note both are the LATEST members of the daily wave by cron (20 6 and 45 6 local), and both are
projects whose bar-raise reads MANY repos - which is a hypothesis, not a finding.

Not "may a stamped-but-unspawned run advance nextRunAt" (that framing assumed consumption, which is

items.prompt:
cd X:\YesAndChains first. CHAINS P2 (2026-07-30 canonical audit, finding 2).

tools/repo_metadata.json declares itself the single source of truth for the GitHub About panel, and tools/update_repo_metadata.py PATCHes the repo from it. But the live About panel was edited through the GitHub UI at some point and is now AHEAD of the checked-in copy on two of three fields.   homepage     JSON: https://theprophetkane.github.io/yesandchains/
               live: https://yesandchains.com          <- live is right
  topics       JSON: 10 topics
               live: 14 (adds mobile-first, offline-first, progressive-web-app,
                     sports-app)                       <- live is right
  description  JSON: '...AI recommender (in design)...'
               live: '...get AI-powered disc recommendations.'
                                                       <- JSON is right; live
                     promises a surface CHAINS_VISIBLE=false hides

So the reconciliation is not one-directional. Take homepage and the four extra topics UP from live into repo_metadata.json; keep the honest '(in design)' description and let the sync push that one DOWN. Do not run the sync script before reconciling the JSON.

Worth considering as part of the same pass: the script currently has no 'live is ahead' concept at all, it just overwrites. A --check mode that reports drift in both directions and refuses to PATCH when live carries a value the JSON does not would stop this recurring. That is the durable fix; the field reconciliation is the immediate one.

items.evidence: No docs/CANONICAL_AUDIT-2026-07-29.md exists (the 2026-07-29 routine blackout, already diagnosed as host memory exhaustion in queue item loop-tick-2026-07-29-barraise-runs-produce-no-output). Through all of 07-29 and most of 07-30, X:\YesAndEverything\status\data\Chains.json carried audit.latestReportAt 2026-07-28T06:49:06Z and the dashboard rendered those counts with no age signal. tools/audit_dashboard.py's _warn_unparsed guard (:233-250, added 0.58.1) fires only when a report parses badly, never when no report arrives.
items.prompt:
cd X:\YesAndChains first. CHAINS P2 (2026-07-30 canonical audit, finding 3).

The nightly audit chain skipped 2026-07-29 (host memory exhaustion, root cause already tracked separately). The gap itself is not the problem. The problem is that nothing anywhere signalled it: status/data/Chains.json kept serving audit.latestReportAt of 2026-07-28T06:49:06Z, and the dashboard renders those findings counts identically whether they are eight hours or eight days old.

This is the same class of defect the 0.58.1 _warn_unparsed guard was written to close. That guard's stated principle in its own docstring is 'better to break the caller than to publish a confident zero'. It only covers the case where a report exists and parses badly. A report that never arrives publishes a confident STALE number, which is the same failure wearing a different hat.

Add a freshness assertion on audit.latestReportAt. Suggested shape, matching the existing guard's style:
  - warn (non-fatal) past roughly 36 hours
  - fail past roughly 72 hours
  - surface the age on the dashboard itself so a human reading it can see the counts are stale without opening the JSON

Put the assertion where it will actually run even when the nightly does not. If it lives only inside audit_dashboard.py sync, a night where no routine fires also means no freshness check fires, which reproduces the bug. The dashboard render side, or a separate cheap watchdog, is the right home.

Note when scoping: the same reasoning applies to every project's status JSON, not just Chains. Chains is where it was caught. Decide whether to fix it here first or go straight to the shared surface.
