items.title: Six of seven system_settings keys are inert: M8's admin-configurable knobs are a UI over numbers nothing reads
items.evidence: Six of the seven system_settings keys have no consumer anywhere in the codebase. Searched every key by bare name across apps/api/src, apps/web/src and packages/shared/src, excluding tests and lib/settings.ts (which only defines defaults and does the load/save round-trip). Only max_hours_per_day reaches behavior: routes/schedule.ts passes it into fillSchedule, where isEligible gates per-day hours. The other six appear ONLY as three lines each in apps/web/src/routes/AdminSettings.tsx (read into state, send back on save, render the input) plus a type field in packages/shared/src/index.ts. What each should drive, and what actually drives it: preference_window_weeks and preference_freeze_days -- preferenceWindow() in packages/shared/src/dates.ts:95-107 takes no settings argument and hardcodes addDays(today, 8) and addDays(today, 49); both call sites (Home.tsx:133, Preferences.tsx:30) pass only today, so an admin setting the window to 4 weeks still gets a 6-week form. time_off_min_notice_days and time_off_max_consecutive_days -- POST /api/time-off validates ISO date shape, end>=start and the type enum and nothing else (time-off.ts:60-73); the strings 'notice' and 'consecutive' do not appear in the file, so these two were never hardcoded, they were never implemented. default_max_employees_per_shift -- template create binds body.max_employees directly (shift-templates.ts:217) and validation only requires max>=min; the default 2 comes from the SQL column default (0003:51, 0004:12), and the SPA never reads the key so there is not even a form prefill. ideal_hours_per_day -- schedule-fill.ts reads exactly two config fields, max_hours_per_day and max_shifts_per_day; the algorithm has no ideal-hours term. DESIGN section 21's M8 entry calls these 'four previously-hardcoded policy knobs exposed as system_settings keys' under a milestone titled 'Admin-configurable shift options' -- the hardcodes were never removed. The doc also contradicted itself: section 7.1 states the window as fixed literals (correct, matches code) while section 15 called the same two numbers admin-tunable. Four prior audits verified the section and passed it, because the section is not wrong about anything it says -- all seven keys exist in the migration, in section 15's list, in the shared types, and in the settings UI. Presence is not wiring.
items.fix: Pick one of two coherent outcomes; this is a product decision, not a text fix. (a) WIRE THEM: thread preference_window_weeks and preference_freeze_days into preferenceWindow() as parameters (it is in packages/shared, so both the SPA callers and any server-side check get them from one place), add the two time-off validations to POST /api/time-off, read default_max_employees_per_shift as the template-form default, and either give ideal_hours_per_day a soft-preference term in the auto-fill or drop the key. Note that wiring the window makes it a settings read on a hot SPA path, so decide where the value is fetched. (b) RETIRE THEM: mark the keys reserved-not-yet-enforced in DESIGN section 15 and section 21, and remove the inputs from /admin/settings so the UI stops implying they do something. The 2026-07-30 drift pass already landed the interim honesty labelling in DESIGN section 15 (a new 'Only one of the seven keys is enforced' paragraph), section 21's M8 entry, section 3.2, section 3.3, section 7.1 and section 8.1, so the doc no longer overstates -- but CLAUDE.md:26 still repeats the M8 'four policy knobs exposed as system_settings keys' claim and needs the same qualification. Handler files are never auto-edited, so that line is left for an attended session.

items.title: Section 11's swap coworker hour-cap eligibility is enforced in neither the API nor the SPA
items.evidence: DESIGN section 11 says employee A 'picks an eligible coworker B (same sub-department, not already at hour cap)'. POST /api/change-requests with type:swap checks exactly three things about the target (change-requests.ts:118-142): target_user_id is a positive integer, it is not the requester, and a user_sub_departments row joins the target to the shift's sub-department. The strings max_hours and hour appear nowhere in the 16KB file -- not at offer time, not at the target's accept (:319-352), not at manager approval (:424-461). The SPA does not compensate: MySchedule.tsx:161-164 builds the coworker list as members.filter(u => u.id !== user.id && u.sub_department_ids.includes(s.sub_department_id)), the same two conditions minus the cap. So the cap is a documented eligibility rule with no implementation on either side of the wire. Practical effect: an approved swap can push B over max_hours_per_week, and the auto-fill then treats that as immovable existing load on the next generate (schedule.ts:88-93), quietly starving B of assignments in a later week rather than surfacing the overrun.
items.fix: Either implement the check or strike the clause. If implementing: filter the offer-time coworker list and re-check at accept, because hours can change between offer and acceptance (a 48-hour TTL window is plenty of time for the target to pick up an open shift). The weekly-hours figure to compare against is the same one the auto-fill uses -- users.max_hours_per_week -- and the shift's own hours come from hoursBetween(start_time, end_time) in schedule-fill.ts, which handles the overnight wrap; do not reimplement that arithmetic. items.title: google.ts infers the calendar id from SKYLIGHT_EMAIL, which DESIGN section 8 forbids by name
items.detail: src/google.ts:25 calId() reads: return encodeURIComponent(env.GOOGLE_CALENDAR_ID || env.SKYLIGHT_EMAIL || "primary"). That middle term infers the target Google calendar from the Skylight LOGIN account, which DESIGN.md section 8 forbids by name: "The frame reads livinwithloynds, NOT the Skylight login account... The two are independent -- never infer one from the other." The two accounts really are different: the Skylight app account is theprophetkane@gmail.com and the calendar the frame syncs is LivinWithLoynds@gmail.com. The fallback is unreachable today because GOOGLE_CALENDAR_ID is set in wrangler.jsonc:61, so this is latent rather than live. But the failure mode if it were ever unset is the worst one this project has: createEvent would POST to theprophetkane's calendar, Google would return 200 with an event id, quickAdd would report success, and the event would never appear on the wall -- indistinguishable from success in the API response, the UI and the email confirmation. src/owners.ts:52 calendarFor() does the equivalent fallback chain correctly (owner var -> GOOGLE_CALENDAR_ID -> "primary", no SKYLIGHT_EMAIL), so calId() is the odd one out. calId() is reached by google.probe() and by createEvent whenever no calendarId is passed. The fix is to delete " || env.SKYLIGHT_EMAIL" so the chain matches owners.ts. That is a one-token edit but it is still a behaviour change on a repo a parallel session owns, which is why the nightly routine queued it instead of applying it.
items.evidence: src/google.ts:25 (the fallback); src/owners.ts:52 (the correct chain, for contrast); DESIGN.md section 8 lines 211-217 (the rule it violates, plus the 2026-07-25 verification that the two accounts are independent); wrangler.jsonc:61 (GOOGLE_CALENDAR_ID is set, which is why this is latent). src/types.ts:5 types SKYLIGHT_EMAIL as a required secret even though DESIGN.md section 8 records it was never deployed -- so the fallback would resolve to undefined in practice and land on "primary", which for a service account is the service account's own empty calendar. Either way the event leaves the wall.
items.impact: Latent, not live. If GOOGLE_CALENDAR_ID is ever unset or typo'd, every event written through calId() silently leaves the physical wall while reporting success to the family. Silent-wrong is the exact failure class D14 and the whole owner model exist to prevent.

But the failure mode if it were ever unset is the worst one this project has: createEvent would POST to theprophetkane's calendar, Google would return 200 with an event id, quickAdd would report success, and the event would never appear on the wall -- indistinguishable from success in the API response, the UI and the email confirmation. src/owners.ts:52 calendarFor() does the equivalent fallback chain correctly (owner var -> GOOGLE_CALENDAR_ID -> "primary", no SKYLIGHT_EMAIL), so calId() is the odd one out. calId() is reached by google.probe() and by createEvent whenever no calendarId is passed. The fix is to delete " || env.SKYLIGHT_EMAIL" so the chain matches owners.ts. That is a one-token edit but it is still a behaviour change on a repo a parallel session owns, which is why the nightly routine queued it instead of applying it.

Evidence: src/google.ts:25 (the fallback); src/owners.ts:52 (the correct chain, for contrast); DESIGN.md section 8 lines 211-217 (the rule it violates, plus the 2026-07-25 verification that the two accounts are independent); wrangler.jsonc:61 (GOOGLE_CALENDAR_ID is set, which is why this is latent). src/types.ts:5 types SKYLIGHT_EMAIL as a required secret even though DESIGN.md section 8 records it was never deployed -- so the fallback would resolve to undefined in practice and land on "primary", which for a service account is the service account's own empty calendar. Either way the event leaves the wall.

What to do: remove the " || env.SKYLIGHT_EMAIL" term from calId() in src/google.ts:25 so the fallback chain reads GOOGLE_CALENDAR_ID -> "primary", matching calendarFor() in src/owners.ts:52. Consider whether calId() should instead throw when GOOGLE_CALENDAR_ID is missing rather than falling through to "primary" -- for a service account "primary" is its own empty calendar, which is another silent-success path, so a thrown error may be the better contract. If you change that, record it as a DESIGN.md decision note. Then typecheck (npx tsc --noEmit).

items.detail: The nightly audit found Mizzium, a secret: true entity, shipping on the public /lore/the-aestral-economy page because web/build.mjs hardcoded { k: "mizzium", n: "Mizzium", tier: "offmarket" } into the CHIP_METALS ladder. items.title: Rewrite _ring_cells as a four-edge perimeter walk into a reused member Array so a ring costs O(8r) instead of O((2r+1)^2) with no allocation.
items.evidence: source/world3d/enemy_field_3d.gd:435-443 _ring_cells builds ring r by iterating the whole (2r+1)^2 square and filtering with maxi(abs(dx), abs(dz)) == r, allocating a fresh Array each call. nearest_index (:295-321) calls it once per ring and only breaks after a candidate is found; unit_controller.gd:154 calls nearest_index per unit per tick. _max_ring is 30 at campaign map_extent 110 (:237) and wave_director.gd:68 spawns at map_extent * 0.92, so the nearest candidate first appears around ring 13, costing about 3,650 square iterations plus 14 Array allocations per unit per tick.

items.title: The shipped default rule pack outranks every rule the user saves through the Categorize UI, and its unanchored substring alternations match inside unrelated words, so 29 transactions sit under a perma
items.impact: The shipped default rule pack outranks every rule the user saves through the Categorize UI, and its unanchored substring alternations match inside unrelated words, so 29 transactions sit under a permanently unreachable user rule and 4 already carry a wrong category on disk.
items.detail: packages/shared/src/default-rules.ts:6-7 states lower wins first, brand matches at priority 50 and generic token matches at 200 so brand rules always win, and the sub() and re() helpers at :20,:28 default to 50. But every rule the primary UI creates is hardcoded to 100 (server.ts:487 and :628, body.priority ?? 100; Categorize.tsx:75 never passes a priority), so the user's most-specific rule always loses to the starter pack. Live ledger: 3 merchant strings covering 29 tx (4.5 percent of 649) have a verbatim user rule shadowed by a lower-priority seed rule pointing at a different category, including ANTHROPIC ANTHROPIC COMCA (26 tx, user rule to Personal Projects at 100, shadowed by a 50 seed rule to Subscriptions). The unanchored alternations also produce 34 sub-word matches across 27 distinct merchant strings, and 4 rows already carry a wrong category: BATTERIES PLUS CREVE COEUR reads Utilities via ATT inside BATTERIES; GOOGLE WORKSPACE_YESA reads Personal Care via SPA inside WORKSPACE; BKOFAMERICA MOBILE DEPOSIT MOBILE twice reads Utilities via T MOBILE spanning DEPOSI[T MOBILE]. No rule anywhere uses priority 200; observed max is 150.

items.title: The stderr-hardening that cost three releases their dashboard-write step on 2026-07-24 is only half closed: 2>$null throws a terminating NativeCommandError under EAP Stop exactly as 2>&1 does, and nin
items.impact: The stderr-hardening that cost three releases their dashboard-write step on 2026-07-24 is only half closed: 2>$null throws a terminating NativeCommandError under EAP Stop exactly as 2>&1 does, and nine git reads across all four release scripts still use it.
items.detail: Probed on this machine (PS 5.1.19041.6456, ANSI cp Windows-1252): under $ErrorActionPreference='Stop' a native command writing stderr with 2>$null raises NativeCommandError, 2>&1 raises it, and an unredirected call does not. EAP Stop is set at release.ps1:34, push-to-github.ps1:17, write-dashboard-status.ps1:12. Nine surviving 2>$null git reads: release.ps1:46; push-to-github.ps1:46; write-dashboard-status.ps1:40,41,42,48,99,247,261; git-guard.ps1:81. git-guard.ps1:27-29 warns only about 2>&1 and Invoke-Git (:30-39, added v0.14.10) wraps only add, commit and push, so v0.14.9 and v0.14.10 closed the write half and left the read half. The trigger is live: core.autocrlf true plus .gitattributes *.ps1 text eol=crlf while git ls-files --eol scripts/ shows 11 of 13 files as w/lf and one w/mixed, so git emits normalization warnings to stderr on status, diff and add against these paths.

items.title: Agents: both live Agents routine files instruct a blind Remove-Item on .git\index.lock, which CLAUDE.md:30 forbids by name
items.evidence: C:\Users\Kane\.claude\scheduled-tasks\bar-raise-agents\SKILL.md:13 says 'if X:\YesAndAgents\.git\index.lock exists and is older than ~10 minutes, remove it', and audit-agents-nightly\SKILL.md:20 says 'Before any git work, clear a stale .git\index.lock (older than ~10 min)'. X:\YesAndAgents\CLAUDE.md:30 forbids exactly this: it mandates dot-sourcing scripts/git-guard.ps1 and calling Assert-GitSafe, and permits a hand-rm only after Get-Process git is empty AND the timestamp is stale. The routine instructions check age but never process liveness, so a live git process holding the lock at the ten-minute mark gets it deleted underneath, which is the documented NUL-corruption path on this FUSE mount. Both routines run unattended nightly against a repo that other routines also touch. Same class as canonical-audit-2026-07-24-agents-script-route-blind-lock-delete, different layer (routine instructions, not server.mjs).
items.prompt:
Agents MEDIUM (bar-raise 2026-07-30): the two live Agents scheduled-routine files tell the routine to blind-delete the git index lock, which the project handler forbids by name.

C:\Users\Kane\.claude\scheduled-tasks\bar-raise-agents\SKILL.md line 13 reads 'Before any git work, if X:\YesAndAgents\.git\index.lock exists and is older than ~10 minutes, remove it (stale lock from a crashed prior run).' C:\Users\Kane\.claude\scheduled-tasks\audit-agents-nightly\SKILL.md line 20 reads 'Before any git work, clear a stale .git\index.lock (older than ~10 min).'

X:\YesAndAgents\CLAUDE.md line 30 says the opposite in as many words: never blind-Remove-Item the lock, because concurrent unattended routines mean a live git process may hold it and deleting it under one corrupts the index. It mandates dot-sourcing scripts/git-guard.ps1 and calling Assert-GitSafe (which clears only a stale lock and aborts on a live race), and allows a hand-rm only after Get-Process git comes back empty AND the lock timestamp is stale. An age check alone does not test liveness: a git process that has held the lock for eleven minutes satisfies the routine's condition.

Fix: replace the blind-delete sentence in both SKILL.md files with 'Before any git work, dot-source X:\YesAndAgents\scripts\git-guard.ps1 and call Assert-GitSafe; do not hand-delete .git\index.lock.' Check the other per-project routine files for the same sentence while you are in there and report which ones carry it, but only edit the two Agents ones under this item.

Both files are outside X:\YesAndAgents, so this edits C:\Users\Kane\.claude\scheduled-tasks\ and touches no project code. Do not change anything else in either file, and do not re-enable or edit the disabled bar-raise-yaag folder.

Why it matters here specifically: Agents' bar-raise reports are gitignored and pruned to newest-of-type, and Steps 7 and 8 (the status JSON write) are skipped for this project by the routine's own instruction, so the in-report run-state table is the only place the review history survives. A skipped day is therefore invisible and unrecoverable rather than merely late.

What to do: this is a diagnosis item, not a code fix. Determine whether the 07-29 run was never spawned, spawned and died, or ran and failed to write. Check the scheduled-task session records (they carry scheduledTaskId plus error/errorCategory; presence means spawned, lastRunAt does not prove it ran) and the routine session transcripts for 2026-07-29 around 11:30Z to 13:00Z. Then either report the cause, or if the fleet is simply oversubscribed at the 11:30Z slot, propose a spread for the daily bar-raise cron times.

cd X:\YesAndApothecary first. Bar-raise 2026-07-30 (HIGH): make a skipped daily review visible on the dashboard.

What happened: the bar-raise-apothecary scheduled task recorded lastRunAt 2026-07-29T12:10:46Z and produced nothing. No docs/BAR_RAISE-2026-07-29.md was written, X:\YesAndEverything\status\data\Apothecary.json never advanced past 2026-07-28T12:05:00Z, and no queue rows were dated 2026-07-29. The dashboard kept publishing stale: false the whole time, so a full missed day of review looked identical to a healthy day.

The root cause of the skip is host-side and is already owned by the portfolio item loop-tick-2026-07-29-barraise-runs-produce-no-output. Do NOT try to fix the scheduler here. Fix the blindness.

In scripts/write-dashboard-status.ps1: derive a review-freshness signal from barRaise.latestReportAt the same way the release-age signal is derived from lastReleaseAt, and publish it. Suggested shape: a barRaise.stale boolean set when latestReportAt is older than 36 hours (one daily slot plus margin), or a barRaiseAgeHours integer the dashboard can band. Pick one and write down why in the commit.

Two constraints. First, the writer already reads the existing JSON to carry barRaise forward; do not let the new field get carried forward stale, recompute it every run from the timestamp. Second, keep the output quiet when everything is fresh, per the solo-tool-ux preference for a dashboard that does not cry wolf. A field that reads false on a healthy day is right; a banner is not.

Verify by hand-setting latestReportAt back two days in a scratch copy and confirming the field flips.

items.title: Cattery rate limiting is a no-op binding while three surfaces report it as on
items.prompt: X:\YesAndCattery\wrangler.jsonc:40-49 records a MEASURED result: repeated calls on a single key against a 30/60s cap all returned success:true, so the API_RATE_LIMITER binding is not enforcing. Cause is a version pin: rate limiting went GA in Sept 2025 and wants a top-level "ratelimits" array, but wrangler 3.114.17 (pinned) does not know that key, warns "Unexpected fields" and drops the binding entirely, so the legacy unsafe.bindings shape at :50-54 is kept deliberately. items.title: Gnosis leaks all 12 secret entity names publicly via preview.json and the nav menu
items.prompt:
Two outlets for one problem in X:\YesAndGnosis. Fix together; fixing only the menu leaves the easier leak open.

(1) preview.json, the worse of the two. GET https://gnosis.yesandeverything.com/preview.json returns 200, 244,011 bytes, 768 entries, of which 12 carry dm:true along with the entity NAME, URL and SUBTYPE. Verified live anonymously 2026-08-02. The subtypes are the damaging part: 'Ruin - Infernal Horizon | campaign arc', 'Infernal Tide - Session Prep | session prep', 'Mizzium | metal', 'DM Plans | future plans', 'The Arcana Stones | future plans', 'The Unchained | faction', four npcs, two references. A player learns the campaign arc name from one static JSON fetch, no view-source needed. This was previously rated LOW as 'gives gated entities their subtype'; that was backwards, it carries MORE than the menu leak does.

(2) The nav menu. Every public page ships all 12 names in its HTML. web/build.mjs:1783 renders them with class=menu-dm, hidden only by the CSS rule at web/build.mjs:734 which sets display:none on .menu-dm for any document whose html element does not carry data-dm=1. Verified live: /lore/the-aestral-economy returns 188,114 bytes with 37 menu-dm occurrences and every sampled secret name present in the served bytes. web/build.mjs:1752 claims a player never sees these, which is a guarantee CSS cannot give: view-source, reader mode, a text-only browser, or CSS failing to load all reveal them.

FIX SHAPE: build the DM set client-side after DM auth, or emit public bundles with the gated entries stripped and inject them on authentication. Keep the gate server-side rather than cosmetic.

NOT the problem: the page gate itself. Anonymous requests to /characters/kazo/, /factions/the-unchained/ and /lore/dm-plans/ all return 401, verified the same run. What leaks is the existence, name and type of each secret, not its content.

items.title: 19 scripts across 9 repos blind-delete a git lock before their own guard can see it
items.prompt:
Nineteen scripts across nine repos blind-delete a git lock, and in fifteen of them Assert-GitSafe runs AFTER the delete, so the guard can only ever see a directory the script already cleaned. Four have no guard call at all. Most are write-dashboard-status.ps1 copies running inside Push-Location on the YesAndEverything root, so they delete locks in the SHARED YaE tree that every project's release writes to and that concurrent unattended routines touch constantly. Deleting a lock under a live git process is the failure that previously NUL-truncated .git/config and dropped refs/heads/main from loose refs.

MEASURED 2026-08-02. Scripts with the pattern, with the line of the Remove-Item and of the first Assert-GitSafe:
  BrackishRising/scripts/publish-gdd.ps1            rm 260, assert 269
  BrackishRising/scripts/release.ps1                rm 57,  NO ASSERT
  BrackishRising/scripts/write-dashboard-status.ps1 rm 230, assert 235
  HereBeHordes/scripts/sync-erik-branch.ps1         rm 23,  assert 23 (same line, check by hand)
  HereBeHordes/scripts/write-dashboard-status.ps1   rm 234, assert 239
  YesAndAgents/scripts/write-dashboard-status.ps1   rm 133, assert 135
  YesAndApothecary/scripts/write-dashboard-status.ps1 rm 240, assert 250
  YesAndCattery/scripts/write-dashboard-status.ps1  rm 107, NO ASSERT
  YesAndChains/scripts/sync-audit-to-dashboard.ps1  rm 59,  assert 64
  YesAndChains/scripts/write-dashboard-status.ps1   rm 271, assert 276
  YesAndEverything/scripts/apply-repo-cleanup.ps1   rm 33,  assert 33 (same line)
  YesAndEverything/scripts/collect-usage.ps1        rm 1148, assert 1155
  YesAndEverything/scripts/consolidate-audit-files.ps1 rm 40, assert 40 (same line)
  YesAndEverything/scripts/estimate-usage-backfill.ps1 rm 70, assert 192
  YesAndEverything/scripts/migrate-ids-to-words.ps1 rm 51,  NO ASSERT
  YesAndEverything/scripts/release-all.ps1          rm 103, NO ASSERT
  YesAndRing/scripts/push-to-github.ps1             rm 19,  assert 50  (deletes its OWN repo lock, least guarded)
  YesAndRing/scripts/write-dashboard-status.ps1     rm 120, assert 123
  YesAndScheduler/scripts/write-dashboard-status.ps1 rm 243, assert 251

FIX: delete the Remove-Item block in each and let Assert-GitSafe adjudicate. The reference shape is YesAndApothecary/scripts/deploy-to-yae.ps1:30-32, which carries a comment saying a robocopy-only script has no business touching YaE's .git and that lock handling belongs to Assert-GitSafe in the script that actually writes. YesAndScheduler/scripts/push-to-github.ps1:22-24 and YesAndAgents/scripts/push-to-github.ps1:12 are the already-fixed examples to copy.

CAUTION on the three 'same line' entries: those may be the guard's own internal delete inside git-guard.ps1's Assert-GitSafe, which is legitimate. Read each before editing.

RELATED, do not duplicate work: bar-raise-2026-07-24-scheduler-audit-sync-blind-lock-delete and canonical-audit-2026-07-25-scheduler-git-lock-guard-defeated already cover the Scheduler instances. The 2026-07-31 Invoke-Git batch fixed the STDERR half of this problem portfolio-wide and left the lock half; several of its commit messages read as though the lock issue was closed.

items.title: audit_dashboard.py sync writes an absolute latestReportPath when given an absolute docs_dir, so a caller outside the repo silently publishes an unusable pointer
items.evidence: tools/audit_dashboard.py latest_report() at line 194 builds rel by taking the glob path and replacing backslashes, so rel is only repo-relative when docs_dir was passed relative. Called as `sync(json, r'X:\HereBeHordes\docs')` it wrote latestReportPath = 'X:/HereBeHordes/docs/CANONICAL_AUDIT-2026-08-03.md' into status/data/Hordes.json instead of 'docs/CANONICAL_AUDIT-2026-08-03.md'. Reproduced twice on 2026-08-03 and corrected both times by re-running with cwd set to the repo and docs_dir='docs'. The status page resolves the pointer against the project repo, so an absolute value does not resolve for any reader. Both in-repo callers (sync-audit-to-dashboard.ps1, write-dashboard-status.ps1) pass the relative default and are unaffected; the exposure is cross-repo callers such as the nightly sweep.
items.prompt: cd X:\YesAndChains first. In tools/audit_dashboard.py, latest_report() returns `rel` as the raw glob path with backslashes normalised, which is only repo-relative when the caller passed a relative docs_dir. A cross-repo caller passing an absolute docs_dir publishes an absolute latestReportPath that the status page cannot resolve. Fix latest_report() (or sync()) to derive `rel` relative to the repo root that contains docs_dir, e.g. os.path.relpath(full, repo_root) with forward slashes, so the pointer is repo-relative regardless of how docs_dir was passed. Add a test covering both a relative and an absolute docs_dir. Do not change the canonical JSON format or any other field of the audit block.

items.title: Chains dashboard audit findings-count writer reports 0/0/0/0 against a real 10-finding report
items.detail: status/data/Chains.json's audit.findings block has read {critical:0,high:0,medium:0,low:0} for at least the last two nightly passes, while docs/CANONICAL_AUDIT-2026-08-05.md (and the 08-04 report before it) carries 10 numbered carried findings. Whatever writes Chains' findings counts into the dashboard JSON either isn't running for this project or is silently zeroing the block. Tonight's audit-pointer refresh only touches latestReportPath/latestReportAt by design and does not correct findings counts, so this has been carried unfixed across passes. Needs someone to find and fix the writer (likely the same class of bug as the Budget dashboard-writer zeros fix from e2a6f47, but confirm before assuming the same root cause).
items.prompt:
CHAINS LOW P2 (source: nightly-sweep 2026-08-05): Chains dashboard audit findings-count writer reports 0/0/0/0 against a real 10-finding report.

status/data/Chains.json's audit.findings block reads {critical:0,high:0,medium:0,low:0} while the actual canonical-doc audit report carries 10 numbered carried findings. Find whatever writes this project's findings counts (check scripts/write-dashboard-status.ps1 or equivalent in X:\YesAndChains) and confirm whether it's not running, misparsing the report's severity tags, or silently zeroing on some condition. Compare against Budget's e2a6f47 fix (a similar zeros bug) but verify the root cause before assuming it's identical. Fix the writer so it reflects the report's actual severity counts, then re-verify against the current CANONICAL_AUDIT report.
